Dana — thanks for the clear asks and the forecast. High level thoughts from our side: 

1) Co-term + multi-year ramp: we can do an 18-month co-term that starts on your requested Oct 1 date. That lets us align billing and simplifies reporting.

2) Triggered bumps: we propose three explicit threshold triggers (60%, 85%, 110% of committed monthly tokens) that automatically unlock short-term burst capacity at a pre-agreed uplift rate. Triggers would be measured on a 30-day trailing average.

3) Opt-out / safety valve: a 60-day review window after any triggered bump where Helix can request an adjustment. If usage drops below 50% of the bumped level for two consecutive months, we offer a one-time de-escalation with prorated credits.

Next steps I suggest: I’ll draft a short amendment with the ramp schedule, trigger definitions, pricing ladder, and the opt-out mechanics. Can Marissa and Karthik weigh in on SLA impacts and billing cadence? Priyom, bringing you in for the implementation sequencing (can we support Oct 1 start given on-boarding lead time?).

I’ll attach a sketch amendment by EOD tomorrow.

—Rafael
